corpus_definition: To be careful because something bad might happen.
particle_note: Not separable, no object: "Watch out!"; with a thing: "watch out for + noun": "watch out for cars".

relations.note: Same meaning, also used as a warning: "Look out!"

context.text: Watch out! The floor is wet. In winter you also have to watch out for ice on the roads in Tashkent.

corpus_definition: A place on the internet with pages about a topic.

forms.definition: a group of pages on the internet about one topic or company
forms.example: Check our website for more information.

syn.note: Short, very common form.
One page of a website.

context.text: You can buy train tickets on the railway website. The website also shows the times of all trains.

reviewer_note: Headword is itself a compound; no family forms.

corpus_definition: How heavy something or someone is.

forms.definition: how heavy a person or thing is
forms.example: The weight of the bag is ten kilos.

syn.note: The quality of being heavy.
Scientific word for the amount of matter.

forms.definition: to measure how heavy something is, or to have a certain heaviness
forms.example: The baby weighs four kilos.

syn.note: Find the size or amount of something.

forms.definition: heavier than is healthy or allowed
forms.example: The doctor said I was a little overweight.

syn.note: Polite, general word.
Direct and can be rude.

ant.note: Having little fat on the body.

forms.definition: serious and important
forms.example: They discussed weighty matters.
forms.note: Belongs to weight = importance, not heaviness. Formal.

context.text: At the market the seller weighs the melons. He tells you the weight and then the price.

reviewer_note: weighty = serious, so other_meaning. weigh is the verb by meaning.

corpus_definition: a common grain used to make bread and pasta

forms.definition: a plant whose grain is used to make flour for bread
forms.example: Farmers in Kashkadarya grow a lot of wheat.

syn.note: Seeds of plants like wheat and rice.
Another grain, used for food and drinks.

context.text: In June the wheat fields near our village turn gold. Farmers cut the wheat and take it to the mill.

reviewer_note: No family forms; wholewheat is a compound.

corpus_definition: a high clear sound made by blowing air through lips or a tool

forms.definition: a high sound made by blowing, or a small thing you blow to make it
forms.example: The referee blew his whistle.

syn.note: A short sound from a horn.

forms.definition: to make a high sound by blowing through your lips
forms.example: My dad whistles when he is happy.

syn.note: Sing with your mouth closed.

context.text: The football coach blows a whistle to start practice. Then he whistles loudly when someone scores.

corpus_definition: A technology that lets computers connect to the web without cables.

forms.definition: a way to connect to the internet without cables
forms.example: Is there free wifi in this cafe?

syn.note: Full, more formal name.
A place or phone that gives wifi.

context.text: The wifi at our school is very slow. Students go to the cafe next door because its wifi is free.

corpus_definition: Living or growing in nature, not kept by humans.

forms.definition: the quality of being natural and not controlled
forms.example: I love the wildness of the mountains.

forms.definition: a large natural area where no people live
forms.example: They got lost in the wilderness.

forms.definition: living or growing in nature, not looked after by people
forms.example: We saw wild horses in the mountains.

syn.note: Not made or changed by people.
Not trained to live with people.

ant.note: Kept by people, like cats and cows.

forms.definition: in a very excited or uncontrolled way
forms.example: The fans cheered wildly.
forms.note: Belongs to wild = out of control, not living in nature.

context.text: In the Chatkal mountains you can see wild goats. The wildness of this place attracts many tourists.

reviewer_note: wildly is the out-of-control sense; wildlife is a compound, left out.

corpus_definition: To clean a surface by rubbing it with a cloth.

forms.definition: a quick clean with a cloth, or a small wet cloth
forms.example: Give the table a quick wipe.

forms.definition: to clean something by moving a cloth over it
forms.example: Please wipe the table after dinner.

syn.note: General word.
Move something backwards and forwards on a surface.
Remove water.

people.definition: a moving rubber arm that cleans rain from a car window
people.example: Turn on the wipers, it is raining.

context.text: After lunch Nilufar wipes the table with a cloth. Then she gives the kitchen counter a quick wipe too.

corpus_definition: a thin piece of metal used to carry electricity or hold things

forms.definition: a long thin piece of metal, used for electricity or tying
forms.example: The electrician cut the old wire.

syn.note: Thicker, often covered in plastic.
A covered wire on an electric machine.

forms.definition: all the wires that carry electricity in a building
forms.example: The wiring in this old house is dangerous.

forms.definition: to connect a building or machine to the electricity supply
forms.example: They wired the new kitchen last week.

syn.note: Join something to electricity or a network.

forms.definition: working without wires, using radio signals
forms.example: I bought wireless headphones.

syn.note: With no electric cord.

context.text: My grandfather fixed the lamp with a new wire. Now he wants wireless lights in the garden.

reviewer_note: wire = send money is old-fashioned, not covered.

corpus_definition: a person in stories who has magical powers

forms.definition: a man in stories who can do magic
forms.example: The old wizard lived in a tower.

syn.note: A person who does magic, also tricks on stage.
Literary word for a powerful, often bad, wizard.

forms.definition: magic, or great skill at something
forms.example: The film is full of wizardry.

context.text: My little sister loves books about a young wizard. She says his wizardry is better than any film.

reviewer_note: Headword is a person noun, so it stays the main noun entry (rule 6).
